evidence: Start (What happened? and How did we respond?): impact on management operations began 16:50 China Standard Time on 8 Dec 2025. End (What happened? and How did we respond?): all impact confirmed mitigated 02:00 CST on 9 Dec 2025. Regions (What went wrong and why?): every region of the Azure in China cloud was affected because policy data replicates globally.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 12/08/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Times given in CST (UTC+8) and converted. Scope coded global because the report says all regions of the Azure in China cloud were affected; this is limited to that sovereign cloud and no region codes are named, so regions is empty. Many services had recovered by 23:53 CST with residual impact, not stated as most customers, so the 02:00 CST end is used. services_n counts the 23 listed services; the list says not limited to these.

evidence: Start (Timeline of events): impact began when storage scale units shut down from heat at 16:53 UTC, 5 Nov 2025. End (Timeline of events): services back online and impact mitigated 02:25 UTC, 6 Nov 2025. Regions (What went wrong and why?): a datacenter in physical Availability Zone 01 of West Europe overheated.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 11/05/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Start is given as approximately 16:53 UTC in the summary and exactly in the timeline. Zone is the physical zone AZ01 as the report labels it; the report says nothing on the region's other zones. services_n counts VMs, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, MySQL Flexible Server, AKS, Storage, Service Bus, VMSS and Databricks (Unity Catalog and Databricks SQL treated as Databricks features); the list says among others.

evidence: Start (Timeline of major incident milestones): crashes triggered customer impact at 15:41 UTC, 29 Oct 2025. End (Timeline): availability and latency back to normal, impact confirmed mitigated 00:05 UTC, 30 Oct 2025. Regions (What went wrong and why?): the crash spread to every edge site worldwide, giving global platform impact.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 10/29/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. No Azure region named; AFD runs on global edge sites. Some customers saw improvement from 18:30 UTC, not stated as most, so the 00:05 UTC end is used. services_n counts AFD, CDN, 13 listed Azure services and 11 other Microsoft products (Dynamics 365 and Power Platform counted separately); the inability to open support cases is not counted as a product.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): first customer impact at 07:50 UTC, 9 Oct 2025, growing for 90 minutes. End (How did we respond?): AFD availability fully back at 12:50 UTC, with only a subset still seeing latency. Regions (What happened?): impact mainly in Africa and Europe, plus Asia Pacific and the Middle East.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 10/09/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Scope unclear: only geographies (Africa, Europe, Asia Pacific, Middle East) and edge sites are named, no Azure region. End uses 12:50 UTC when availability was restored for most customers; elevated latency for a subset lasted until 16:00 UTC, when the incident was declared mitigated. services_n counts AFD, CDN and the Azure Portal; other unnamed Microsoft management portals are not counted.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): the configuration change triggered impact at 23:54 UTC, 26 Sep 2025. End (How did we respond?): recovery confirmed for most affected services at 04:00 UTC, 27 Sep 2025, with a residual subset. Regions (What went wrong and why?): certificate change hit load balancers in Switzerland North across multiple availability zones.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 09/26/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. End uses 04:00 UTC, when the majority of services recovered and many customers were mitigated; residual impact on a subset of resources lasted until full recovery at 21:59 UTC, 27 Sep 2025. Zones not named individually; the report says multiple availability zones in the region. services_n counts the 24 listed services.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): impact started in AZ03 at 09:03 UTC, 10 Sep 2025. End (What happened? and How did we respond?): Allocator issue mitigated and control plane restored at 18:50 UTC. Regions (What happened?): two physical zones, AZ02 and AZ03, in East US 2 saw degraded management operations.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 09/10/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. End uses 18:50 UTC; later downstream recovery to 19:30 UTC is attributed to backlog drainage and retries, which the rules exclude. AZ03 began at 09:03 UTC and AZ02 began throttling at 10:02 UTC; zone starts are not region starts. AZ01 allocation failures came from existing SKU constraints, not this issue, so AZ01 is not coded. Zones are physical zone labels. services_n counts VMs, VMSS, Backup, Batch, Databricks, Data Factory, AKS, Synapse and Dev Box.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): a fiber cut caused packet loss and impact from 13:37 UTC, 18 Mar 2025. End (How did we respond?): second window mitigated, full mitigation for customers at 00:30 UTC, 19 Mar 2025. Regions (What happened?): East US inter-zone traffic involving AZ03, with minor spread to AZ01 and AZ02 later.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 03/18/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Two impact windows: 13:37 to 16:52 UTC on 18 Mar and 23:20 UTC on 18 Mar to 00:30 UTC on 19 Mar 2025; start and end span both, including the gap. AZ03 was the main zone; AZ01 and AZ02 had minimal inter-zone impact in the second window, hence regional. Zones are physical labels. Fiber restoration completed 06:50 UTC on 19 Mar is not counted. services_n left empty: the report names network connectivity but no specific product as impaired.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): impact began at 16:22 UTC, 3 Mar 2025, when the second redundant device failed. End (How did we respond?): faulty line card isolated and connectivity restored at 18:37 UTC. Regions (What happened?): only the Toronto edge point-of-presence is named as the affected location.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 03/03/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Scope unclear: the Toronto edge PoP is a network edge location, not a named Azure region, so no region code is given. The first device failed at 10:58 UTC without customer impact. services_n counts Microsoft 365, VMs, Storage, App Service, SQL Database, AKS and Azure Portal; the list says not limited to these.

evidence: Start (How did we respond?): DNS records were removed at 16:42 UTC, 25 Feb 2025, with impact building as the TTL expired. End (What happened?): 94 percent of affected customers mitigated by 18:35 UTC. Regions (all sections): no region or geography is named for the authentication failures.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 02/25/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. Onset was gradual as the 5-minute DNS TTL expired after 16:42 UTC. End uses 18:35 UTC, when 94 percent of impacted customers were mitigated; the remainder were mitigated at 01:15 UTC on 26 Feb 2025. Scope unclear: no region named, and the report does not state the impact was global (it only plans to study non-global endpoints). services_n is 1: Microsoft Entra ID, with Seamless SSO and Entra Connect Sync described as its features.

evidence: Start (Timeline of events): impact began after PubSub partitions were recycled at 22:31 UTC, 8 Jan 2025. End (Timeline of events): partitions recovered at 19:18 UTC, 10 Jan, when most customers saw full mitigation. Regions (What happened?): change in physical zone AZ01 of East US 2, with VNet-integrated services hit across zones.
notes: No publication date shown; the header date 01/08/2025 matches the incident date and is not labeled as publication. End uses 19:18 UTC on 10 Jan 2025, when most customers and services saw full mitigation; all services confirmed mitigation at 00:44 UTC on 11 Jan, and AZ01 returned fully to rotation at 04:30 UTC. Coded regional because impact spread beyond AZ01 to multiple zones for zone-redundant VNet-integrated services. Zone is the physical label. services_n counts 18 named services; Private Link with NSGs is described as a customer configuration and not counted.
